title: GDP base-year revision (2015) and the contested back-series
whatChanged: CSO moved the GDP base year from 2004-05 to 2011-12 in January 2015, adopting GVA and SNA 2008 methodology with MCA-21 corporate data. FY2013-14 growth reads 4.7% on the old base but 6.9% on the new. Two conflicting back-series followed in 2018: the NSC Mundle committee version (higher UPA growth, double-digit peaks) and the CSO/NITI Aayog version (lower UPA growth). Arvind Subramanian (2019) argued 2011-17 growth was overstated by ~2.5pp.
bridgeNote: No accepted reconciliation. Instrument policy: carry both series with a visible seam; never splice.

competingAccounts.position: Back-series lowers UPA-era growth; official position
Back-series shows higher UPA growth incl. double-digit years; shelved as 'experimental'
Post-2011 growth overstated ~2.5pp; actual ~4.5% vs official ~7% for 2011-17
Subramanian critique cherry-picked, not statistically robust

title: EUS to PLFS employment survey transition
whatChanged: NSSO Employment-Unemployment Survey (quinquennial, last round 2011-12) replaced by Periodic Labour Force Survey from 2017-18, with changed sampling design and stratification. Pre/post employment comparisons are methodologically contested; no official bridge estimates exist.

title: Withheld 2017-18 Consumer Expenditure Survey
whatChanged: The NSS 2017-18 Household Consumer Expenditure Survey was not released after leaked results indicated declining rural consumption; the government cited data-quality issues. Result: no official consumption-based poverty estimate after 2011-12 until the 2022-23 HCES (itself on a changed methodology).
bridgeNote: 2022-23 HCES uses a modified questionnaire and imputation approach; not comparable with 2011-12 without contested adjustments.

title: Census 2021 not conducted
whatChanged: The decennial census due 2021 was postponed (COVID cited) and has not been conducted as of the project's last update. Every per-capita and rate-based indicator after 2011 rests on population projections, with error compounding over time.

title: WPI-to-CPI inflation regime change
whatChanged: Headline inflation reference shifted from WPI to CPI (combined) around 2013-14; formal CPI inflation targeting (4% +/-2%) adopted 2016 via amended RBI Act. Long-run inflation narratives spanning the change must state which index they use.
bridgeNote: Both indices continue to be published; the break is interpretive, not a data gap.

title: Off-budget borrowing and fiscal accounting
whatChanged: Off-budget devices (FCI food-subsidy bonds, NSSF loans to public entities) understate the headline fiscal deficit in both eras. CAG flagged the practice; a partial clean-up brought FCI dues on-budget in FY2020-21, creating a one-year spike that is an accounting artefact, not a spending surge.
bridgeNote: CAG and budget documents allow partial reconstruction of extended deficit measures.

title: NCRB reporting changes and communal-violence data gaps
whatChanged: NCRB definitional and tabulation changes across editions, plus discontinuation/re-housing of communal-violence reporting between MHA and NCRB, complicate crime and communal-incident trend analysis across 2014.

title: Contested governance indices (RSF, Freedom House, V-Dem)
whatChanged: Third-party democracy/press indices carry their own methodology disputes and periodic recalibrations. Baseline readings circa 2014: RSF rank ~140 (score ~40.3); Freedom House 'Free' (downgrade to 'Partly Free' came 2021); V-Dem liberal-democracy scores higher pre-2014. Recorded as readings, not settled facts; the government contests their methods.

sources.name: RSF World Press Freedom Index archive

title: Peer-country GDP rebasings and WDI vintage drift
whatChanged: Comparator countries revised their own national accounts inside the study window: Vietnam's 2021 rebasing lifted GDP levels ~25%; Bangladesh rebased to 2015-16 with a similar upward level shift. World Bank WDI back-propagates these, so the same query on different dates returns different histories. The peer panel must be pinned to a single WDI vintage, recorded in every series' source.vintage field.
bridgeNote: Pin one WDI vintage for the whole panel; re-pull the entire panel, never one country, when refreshing.

title: Third GDP base-year revision to 2022-23 (released 27 February 2026)
whatChanged: MoSPI released a new national accounts series rebased from 2011-12 to 2022-23, adopting double deflation, a Supply-Use Table framework, and new source data (GST returns, PLFS, ASUSE). It revised recent real growth UP (FY24 8.2% to 7.2%, FY25 6.5% to 7.1%, FY26 estimated 7.6%) while lowering the LEVEL of nominal GDP by roughly 3-4%. The level cut mechanically RAISES every ratio-to-GDP in the project — deficit, debt, exports, GFCF, tax — without any change in underlying activity. Advisory body: ACNAS, chaired by Prof. Biswanath Goldar. 'Sources and Methods' documentation due August 2026.
bridgeNote: Back-series to be spliced at disaggregated level; not yet published. Until it is, FY24 and FY25 have two valid growth figures and every ratio-to-GDP has two valid denominators. Instrument policy: THREE regimes, never one line.

competingAccounts.position: Routine decadal rebasing to a recent normal post-COVID year; methodologically superior (double deflation, SUT, GST-based data)

A rebasing that simultaneously raises growth and lowers the level arrives conveniently; the absence of published Sources and Methods until Aug 2026 makes independent verification impossible in the interim

title: CPI base revision to 2024 (new series from February 2026)
whatChanged: A new CPI series with base year 2024 was introduced, with weights redrawn from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey and a higher non-food weight. Since food inflation drove most headline breaches in 2020 and 2022-23, a lower food weight mechanically dampens future headline volatility relative to the old basket — meaning post-2026 inflation performance is not directly comparable with the 2014-2025 record on which the inflation-targeting verdict rests.
bridgeNote: Weight-effect decomposition would be needed to compare like with like across the break.
notes: Tier-4 sourcing pending a T1 MoSPI press note pull. Flagged in the open verification queue.

title: IIP and WPI base revisions; new Producer Price Index
whatChanged: IIP rebasing to 2022-23 (due around May 2026), a WPI revision in progress, and a planned Producer Price Index. Industrial-production and wholesale-price series will break at these points.

title: Fiscal anchor changes from deficit to debt (from FY2026-27)
whatChanged: From FY27 the Centre shifts its operational fiscal anchor from the annual fiscal-deficit ratio to a debt-to-GDP target (central debt ~56.1% in FY26, glide to 50%±1% by FY31). Fiscal performance before and after FY27 is therefore benchmarked against different objectives. Compounding: P-10 lowered the GDP denominator by 3-4%, which raises measured debt/GDP without any change in borrowing.
bridgeNote: Both measures remain computable; the break is in what counts as success, not in the data.

title: World Bank WDI fiscal-year labelling for India versus calendar years for peers
whatChanged: WDI labels India's fiscal-year observations by the starting calendar year, so WDI '2014' for India corresponds to FY2014-15 (Apr 2014-Mar 2015), while '2014' for Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and China is a different period basis. Peer comparisons drawn straight from WDI therefore compare India's FY with peers' CY, offset by up to nine months — material when a shock (2020 COVID, 2022 commodity spike) lands mid-year. This also explains the apparent conflict between the Phase 1 exports figure (25.4% of GDP, FY2013-14, T1) and WDI's 22.97% for '2014': they are different periods, not contradictory sources.
bridgeNote: State the period basis on every peer chart; never present an India WDI year and a peer WDI year as the same period without the offset noted. VERIFY the WDI India labelling convention against WDI documentation before relying on this record.
notes: Discovered while reconciling Phase 1 and Phase 2 export figures. Convention stated from general knowledge — flagged for primary verification.
